title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 2
statement: While exploring a cave, Carl comes across a collection of \(5\)-pound rocks worth $\(14\) each, \(4\)-pound rocks worth $\(11\) each, and \(1\)-pound rocks worth $\(2\) each. There are at least \(20\) of each size. He can carry at most \(18\) pounds. What is the maximum value, in dollars, of the rocks he can carry out of the cave?

solutions.text:
The rocks are worth $\(2.80,\) $\(2.75,\) and $\(2\) per pound, respectively. For each possible number of \(5\)-pound rocks, use as many \(4\)-pound rocks as fit and fill any leftover capacity with \(1\)-pound rocks. Taking \(0,1,2,\) or \(3\) of the \(5\)-pound rocks gives maximum values $\(48,\) $\(49,\) $\(50,\) and $\(48,\) respectively.

Thus two \(5\)-pound and two \(4\)-pound rocks use all \(18\) pounds, and the maximum value is $\(50.\) Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Compare the value per pound: \(\$2.80,\) \(\$2.75,\) and \(\$2\) for the three rock sizes
Filling the full \(18\) pounds matters more than always grabbing the best per-pound rock; try two \(5\)-pound and two \(4\)-pound rocks
